rationale: Pulp's consent-gated Development Inspector runtime evaluator needs the existing view and accessibility callbacks to remain safe while a request crosses the inspector transport and returns to the UI thread. The retained UI dispatch seams now use lifetime-checked callbacks instead of retaining raw owners across pointer, gesture, drag, and accessibility work; the macOS accessibility provider uses the same explicit host-lifetime token so AppKit cannot call through an already-destroyed bridge. These changes preserve the existing event ordering and accessibility semantics while making teardown and concurrent inspector requests fail closed. This is Pulp-specific developer-tool and host-lifecycle integration with no counterpart framework behavior to backport.
